top_rules: Fix ladder: remove sharing, value/let (weak let 6.3+), @MainActor, sending, Mutex in final class: Sendable, commented actor, per-import @preconcurrency, only then @unchecked Sendable / nonisolated(unsafe).

@unchecked Sendable needs three things: removal test fails (delete the attribute, build, exit 0 means redundant), a visible guard in the body, and an adjacent comment naming the guard. Run the awk reason check on diff-touched files only, since 70% of exemplar hatches have no comment.
A final class whose only stored state is a let Mutex is plain Sendable on 6.3 and 6.4 and never @unchecked. One stray mutable property then errors 'stored property is mutable'.

Shared-state table: Mutex for sync short sections that never suspend, actor only with a 'because' comment, @MainActor for UI and singletons, custom @globalActor niche (3 in the corpus), NIOLockedValueBox only inside the NIO stack.

Published libraries, SDKs, CLIs and servers never set defaultIsolation(MainActor.self). Apps and app-internal UI packages may, with explicit .swiftLanguageMode(.v6). The jq check over dump-package flags exported targets that set it.

Enable NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault by feature name for new libraries, CLIs and servers. Migrate existing code with 'swift package migrate --to-feature'. The change is silent: exit 132 vs 0 at runtime, and wrappers like 'await self.iterator.next()' break. Forward isolation: isolated (any Actor)? = #isolation.

Strip the template's ApproachableConcurrency bundle on every target, test targets included. Three of its five members are already on in Swift 6 mode, 0 exemplar manifests use the name, and the named features say what they do.

A library with public async or protocol API ships a CompileTests package that builds it under defaultIsolation(MainActor) + NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault + InferIsolatedConformances on the floor and current toolchains. Exit 0 is the gate.
surprises: TSan on Linux does catch the unguarded @unchecked plant (exit 1, 3 warnings), but Docker's default seccomp blocks it (needs --security-opt seccomp=unconfined). It also false-positives on a correct Mutex class on both 6.3 and 6.4, so 'TSan green' is no acceptance test for Mutex code.

The 6.4 'swift package init' template drops swiftLanguageModes (6.3 wrote [.v6]) and adds ApproachableConcurrency to test targets. Swift 6 mode is implied by tools 6.4, so a grep for .v6 now misses it.

StrictMemorySafety flags every USE of a nonisolated(unsafe) binding but neither its declaration nor any @unchecked Sendable use. swiftc and SwiftLint are silent on an unguarded @unchecked class that lost 128,131 of 400,000 increments.

@preconcurrency import turns a real SendingRisksDataRace error into nothing, with no warning, and an unneeded one gives no warning either. ExplicitSendable could not be promoted to an error in 4 attempts, so it is a log-reading audit.

A nonisolated library built without NNBD gets an extra error on 6.4 only when a MainActor-default consumer passes an isolated conformance to its async generic. 6.4 also renamed the group to [#RegionIsolation::SendingRisksDataRace].

Thread.isMainThread is false on Linux after hopping off and back to the MainActor, so it is no isolation probe. Runtime isolation traps all exit 132 via _dispatch_assert_queue_fail. A fresh 25-site re-sample puts avoidable @unchecked Sendable at about 36-40%, and only 8 of 25 sites carry a reason comment, so rules must gate new diffs, not whole trees.

top_rules: SW-CONC-T01: every unstructured Task is stored with a reachable cancel, returned or awaited, or written `_ = Task { } // fire-and-forget: reason`; a statement-position `Task {` is the violation (grep, run red/green).

SW-CONC-T02: build with .treatWarning("NoUseUnstructuredThrowingTask", as: .error) (swiftc 6.4 only; tools 6.2+ manifest) AND enable SwiftLint unhandled_throwing_task, because swiftc flags detached/immediate and SwiftLint flags `.cancel()`-consumed handles, disjoint sets.

SW-CONC-T04: the GCD-in-async grep is a mandatory gate (DispatchSemaphore(, MainActor.run, DispatchQueue.main.async, Thread.sleep(, usleep(, sleep(, .wait()), since swiftc 6.3/6.4 only rejects Thread.sleep, NSLock and NSCondition in async code; a semaphore in a main-actor-inherited Task deadlocks deterministically (exit 124).

SW-CONC-T06: continuations are checked, resumed exactly once on every path through a once-guard, wrapped in withTaskCancellationHandler with an isCancelled re-check after storing; leak = exit 124, double resume = exit 132, unsafe gives no diagnostic; tests run under timeout.

SW-CONC-T07: until SE-0526 withDeadline ships (expected 6.5, absent in 6.4) use a structured race that throws its own TimeoutError, never CancellationError, and document that it cannot stop work that ignores cancellation (1 s limit around a blocking read returned at 4000 ms).

SW-CONC-T05: blocking or long CPU work runs off the cooperative pool (dedicated thread, NIOThreadPool.runIfActive, private queue) behind one cancellable continuation whose onCancel wakes the blocked call; the pool is core-count wide (31 blocked tasks pass, 32 hang on 32 cores).

SW-CONC-T11 and T12: AsyncStream always names a bufferingPolicy (default .unbounded grew to 416 MB vs 11 MB for .bufferingNewest(8)); servers use withDiscardingTaskGroup and bound in-flight children (1.09 GB vs 17 MB).

SW-CONC-T09/T10: post-cancellation cleanup is `defer { await withTaskCancellationShield { await x.close() } }` on 6.4+ (awaited defer alone still aborts), resources expose an awaited close()/shutdown(), and deinit never starts a Task.
surprises: LIBDISPATCH_COOPERATIVE_POOL_STRICT=1 is a no-op on Linux (string absent from the 6.4 libdispatch.so; the semaphore plant did not deadlock under it). The real deterministic deadlock is `Task {}` inheriting @MainActor in main.swift; the pool is core-count wide (31 ok, 32 hang). The brief's expected red did not reproduce.

SwiftLint 0.65.1's static Linux binary is built with SWIFTLINT_DISABLE_SOURCEKIT, so custom_rules is skipped with a warning and exit 0 on planted violations. This undermines the map's Q2 default of SwiftLint as an optional custom_rules vehicle and needs an owner decision.

swiftc 6.4 NoUseUnstructuredThrowingTask and SwiftLint unhandled_throwing_task cover disjoint forms (detached/immediate vs `.cancel()`-consumed handle), and unhandled_throwing_task is opt-in; `Task { () throws(Boom) in throw Boom() }` crashes swift-frontend IRGen on both 6.3 and 6.4.

Compiler noasync coverage is only Thread.sleep, NSLock.lock/unlock and NSCondition; DispatchSemaphore.wait, DispatchGroup.wait, sleep/usleep, DispatchQueue.sync and Process.waitUntilExit compile silently in async code on 6.3 and 6.4.

`try? await Task.sleep` inside a loop becomes a hot spin after cancel (about 18,000 iterations in 500 ms) and never ends; `for await` over a cancelled AsyncStream returns normally, indistinguishable from completion.

The containerization Timeout.run shape (also the common agent shape) returns only after blocking work finishes (4000 ms for a 1 s limit) and reports CancellationError; a continuation race returns on time but orphans the work. A round on the cancel-safe thread/poll off-pool helper and on NIOThreadPool.runIfActive as a fleet primitive is warranted.

SW-CONC-15 — Never block a cooperative-pool thread or the main actor in async code: no DispatchSemaphore, group wait, Thread.sleep, sleep or usleep

SW-CONC-23 — Run blocking syscalls and long CPU work off-pool on a Thread, private DispatchQueue or NIOThreadPool behind one cancellable continuation, not DispatchQueue.global or @concurrent
SW-CONC-24 — Return a distinct TimeoutError from a structured ContinuousClock race, never CancellationError; adopt withDeadline only after it ships
SW-CONC-25 — Never read actor state, await, then act on the earlier read; mutate before suspending, re-check after, or park the in-flight Task
SW-CONC-26 — Do not rely on MainActor.assumeIsolated for callbacks off your control; hop with Task { @MainActor }, assert with preconditionIsolated or #isolation, never Thread.isMainThread
SW-CONC-27 — Run swift test --sanitize=thread as an advisory leg only, expect Mutex false positives, keep deterministic count assertions for hatch-guarded types
SW-CONC-28 — Resolve Sendable and isolation diagnostics in fix-ladder order and name the highest applicable rung before adding any hatch

top_rules: Gate is the git-aware triple: git add, then format --in-place, then lint --strict, then git diff --exit-code, over git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard piped to xargs -r -0.
Never report plain swift format lint as a pass: it exits 0 with findings. Always --strict.
Never gate on hand-typed directories: lint --strict -r Source (mistyped) exits 0 even on a red plant; use git ls-files or -r .
Ship the full 43-rule .swift-format generated by the pinned toolchain: a rules block replaces defaults, a partial block silently disables 28 rules.
Shipped config is 4 spaces, 120 columns, with NeverForceUnwrap, NeverUseForceTry and NeverUseImplicitlyUnwrappedOptionals on. Doc rules and UseEarlyExits stay off.
Never chain swift-format with SwiftFormat or swiftlint --fix: 608 lint findings and a red triple after one swiftformat run.
SwiftLint is optional and carries only custom_rules, run from ghcr.io/realm/swiftlint:0.65.1. The static binary skips custom_rules with exit 0, or aborts with 134.
K-07 is 15 verbatim grep -rn entries judged by output, not exit status, with a zero-file canary. Force-unwrap by grep is rejected (1,288 hits); use NeverForceUnwrap.
surprises: A mistyped or missing path operand to swift format lint --strict exits 0 silently, also on the red plant. This earlier looked like exit 1; the exit-1 was from other findings.
swift format --version prints 'main' on 6.4.0 and the docker tag swift:6.3 floats to 6.3.3, so the formatter cannot be pinned or identified by its own version string.
A rules block in .swift-format replaces the defaults instead of overlaying them, and an unknown rule name is only a warning (an error under --strict). An unknown top-level key is silent everywhere.
The Never* rules exempt whole files that import Testing or XCTest, not just @Test functions. containerization turns them on in config but its CI runs format only, so they never run.

swiftlint-static 0.65.1 silently skips custom_rules (exit 0) or aborts with 134 in swiftsyntax mode; only the dynamic binary or official image enforces them. The dynamic binary also fails to load on the swift:6.4 image (libxml2.so.2 missing).
.swift-format-ignore is honoured only by 6.4.0 (IgnoreManager) and is undocumented; 6.3.3 ignores it. Separately, swift-nio HEAD is not a fixed point of the released formatter (7 test files change).

top_rules: SW-GATE-01: gate block, in order: `git ls-files -z -- '*.swift' | xargs -r -0 swift format lint --strict --parallel`; `swift build -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors`; `swift test -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors`; libraries add `swift package diagnose-api-breaking-changes "$BASELINE"` and `swift package plugin generate-documentation --target "$DOCC_TARGET" --warnings-as-errors --analyze` (steps 1-3 run end to end, red on 4 planted violations, green on the twin)

SW-GATE-02: CI warnings gate is the blanket `-Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` on release-toolchain legs only, nightlies exempt, because per-group flags miss ungrouped warnings and groups older toolchains do not know

SW-GATE-05: any per-group `-Werror <Group>` or `.treatWarning` names only groups present on the oldest leg and comes with `UnknownWarningGroup` promoted; a misspelt group exits 0 silently (watched), and NoUsage/VariableNeverMutated/NoUseUnstructuredThrowingTask/UntypedThrows are unknown on 6.3.3

SW-GATE-03/04: never `unsafeFlags(["-warnings-as-errors"])` (remote dependents fail at tools <= 6.1); `.treatAllWarnings(as: .error)` needs tools 6.2, is root-only, and is for pinned-toolchain consumers, not the library default

SW-GATE-09: remote (git/registry) dependency warnings are suppressed by SwiftPM, local path dependency warnings are not; the same dependency turns the blanket flag red as a path dep and green as a git dep (6.3 and 6.4)

SW-GATE-08: every `@diagnose` carries a plain-literal `reason:` (the compiler accepts it without one, silently), sits on the smallest declaration, and is wrapped in `#if hasFeature(SourceWarningControl)` while 6.3 is supported; checked by `grep -rn -F -e '@diagnose(' --include='*.swift' . | grep -v -F -e 'reason:'`
SW-GATE-11: the DocC gate needs `--warnings-as-errors` and a `.spi.yml` with non-empty `documentation_targets`; the shared check-docs.sh exits 0 with no `.spi.yml` even when a symbol link is broken

SW-GATE-14/15: pin every `uses:` to a 40-hex SHA with a version comment and never `@main`; but a pin of swiftlang/github-workflows soundness.yml does not freeze its scripts (checkout has no ref:), so run format/docs/API gates as inline commands

`swift format lint --strict` on a nonexistent directory or file operand exits 0 silently on 6.3 and 6.4, and without --strict findings exit 0; a typo like `Source` for `Sources` is a green format gate

top_rules: SW-TEST-01: new tests are Swift Testing; a diff must not add a file importing XCTest (git diff --diff-filter=A ... | xargs -r grep -l -e 'import XCTest'), existing XCTest suites are left alone.

SW-TEST-03: interop depends on toolchain AND tools version (tc<6.4 none = silent pass, tc6.4+tools<6.4 limited = warning exit 0, tools>=6.4 complete = exit 1), so CI runs env SWIFT_TESTING_XCTEST_INTEROP_MODE=complete on a >=6.4 toolchain; a 6.3 toolchain ignores the variable.

SW-TEST-04/05: no mutable global state in tests (per-test struct-suite state); .serialized only orders tests inside one @Suite or a parameterized @Test, so @Test(.serialized) on a plain test and two separate .serialized suites both still race (planted, exit 1 on 6.3 and 6.4).

SW-TEST-06: flake triage is swift test --no-parallel (the only flag that serializes Swift Testing; --num-workers does not), then swift test --repeat-until fail --maximum-repetitions N on 6.4+ (6.3 exits 64).

SW-TEST-07/08: no .sleep(/usleep(/nanosleep( in Tests/ as synchronisation; wait with await, confirmation() bridged by withCheckedContinuation, or an injected Clock; a fire-and-forget confirmation fails with 'confirmed 0 times'.

SW-TEST-10: crash and precondition tests use await #expect(processExitsWith: .failure) against precondition, not assert (assert is compiled out in -c release and the exit test goes red); never assert on the trap message; capture list [n] needs Swift >=6.3.

SW-TEST-12/13: CLI end-to-end tests run the built executable out of process and assert stdout, stderr and exit status separately, using swift-subprocess 1.0.0 .string(limit:) or temp-file redirection; never Pipe() + waitUntilExit() + read (deadlocks above 64 KiB).

SW-TEST-14/15: gate coverage from the --show-codecov-path JSON filtered to startswith($root + "/Sources/") with jq -e (totals include tests: 37.5% vs 16.7%); run sanitizers as a separate Linux leg with TSan via --sanitize=thread and ASan via --disable-xctest or ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0.
surprises: swift test --no-parallel serializes Swift Testing globally but --num-workers 1 does not, and --help says the default is --no-parallel while Swift Testing runs parallel by default; .serialized never protects across suites (planted red on 6.3 and 6.4), and SWT_EXPERIMENTAL_SERIALIZED_TRAIT_APPLIES_GLOBALLY did not fix the split-suites plant.

TSan on Linux (6.3 and 6.4) reports a false-positive data race on correct Synchronization.Mutex code (actor and NSLock twins are green), which collides with the concurrency guidance preferring Mutex; TSan also dies with an ASLR FATAL under Docker on WSL2 unless seccomp=unconfined, and ASan is red on a clean package from libXCTest leak noise.

.timeLimit(.minutes(n)) rescues cancellation-aware waits at exactly 60.000 s but cannot interrupt withCheckedContinuation or a blocked thread (hung past 300 s), so every e2e leg also needs a CI job-level timeout.

The interop env var is silently ignored by 6.3 toolchains, an invalid value behaves like limited on 6.4.0 (the ST-0021 text says complete), and XCTest-side #expect is an error on a 6.4 toolchain even in limited mode; ST-0021 was amended again in April 2026.

swift-argument-parser's Swift Testing CLI helper (requireExecuteCommand) still uses Pipe-then-waitUntilExit (deadlock above the pipe buffer), merges stderr into stdout, and returns "" on Windows (a vacuous pass); Nuke has 0 XCTest files and 153 Testing files, contradicting the map's 'mixed tree' label and replacing measure{} with a ContinuousClock helper.

top_rules: MP-01: read the floor before editing: `swift package tools-version` plus `dump-package | jq` with `.toolsVersion._version` and `.swiftLanguageVersions`; never `head -1 Package.swift`, never `.swiftLanguageModes`.
MP-02: libraries and the SDK declare tools 6.2, CLIs and servers declare the current release (6.4), nothing new goes below 6.2; raise a library floor only for a feature or dependency that needs it.
MP-03/04: state `swiftLanguageModes: [.v6]` in every manifest; `.v5` only per target, with a same-line dated reason and tracker; never at package level.

MP-05: enable exactly ExistentialAny, MemberImportVisibility, InternalImportsByDefault, NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault and InferIsolatedConformances on every regular, executable and test target; do not use the ApproachableConcurrency bundle or ImmutableWeakCaptures below a 6.3 floor.
MP-06: never list the 15 Swift-6-group names (StrictConcurrency, GlobalConcurrency, ...) in a Swift 6 target; the compiler warns and `.treatAllWarnings(as: .error)` makes it a build break.
MP-07: add `.treatWarning("StrictLanguageFeatures", as: .error)` so misspelt or dead feature names fail the root build; it is root-only and cannot break consumers.

MP-09/10: apply shared settings with one post-definition `for target in package.targets where [...]` loop; no bare `swiftSettings: var`, no `defaultSwiftSettings` (SE-0540 is unshipped); adopt features with `swift package migrate` from a clean tree.

MP-11/12: unsafeFlags only at tools >= 6.2 (below that, version-pinned consumers fail); no `Package@swift-X.swift` by default, and never major-only or patch markers, since an exact marker beats a newer Package.swift; prefer `#if compiler(>=6.4)`.
surprises: The dump-package key is `swiftLanguageVersions`, so the map's M-L-01 jq check (`.swiftLanguageModes`) prints null even when modes are declared. Map conflict 8 is also wrong: service-lifecycle 2.12 is tools 6.1, not 6.2 or later.

`swift package migrate` fails with exit 1 on a bare `swiftSettings: sharedVar`, but only after it has already rewritten the sources, leaving a half-migrated tree. The inline literal, `shared + [...]` and the loop all work on 6.3 and 6.4.

Versioned manifests are a trap. A major-only `Package@swift-6.swift` (tools 6.0) beats a newer Package.swift on every 6.x toolchain, and a versioned file with higher tools shadows Package.swift. The 4 corpus libraries at tools 6.4 carry fallback files that drifted: Alamofire macOS 12 vs 10.13, and swift-dependencies has different dependency URLs and traits.

The tools-version comment may sit on line 2 or 3 since 6.0 (vapor `Package.swift:2`), so `head -1` is unsafe. `swift package tools-version` still works on a toolchain older than the manifest, while `dump-package` errors.

Dead feature names are silently ignored by default. Vapor and async-algorithms list `LifetimeDependence` as upcoming, and three exemplars list `SuppressedAssociatedTypesWithDefaults`, which is unrecognised even as experimental on 6.3 and 6.4. The StrictLanguageFeatures treatWarning guard is root-only, so consumers are unaffected.

Tools 6.3 and 6.4 add almost no manifest API (only `.v27` platform constants and the default `complete` test-interop mode). The 6.4 init template over-floors libraries at 6.4 and drops the explicit language mode. `from:` resolution silently picks an older release on an older toolchain (6.3 got 1.0.0 where 6.4 got 1.1.0). No swift:6.2 image exists here, so the 6.2 floor is verified only through the 6.3 and 6.4 loaders.

top_rules: SW-PKG-D04: a tracked-lockfile repo gates CI three ways: Package.resolved is tracked (git ls-files --error-unmatch), a fresh-scratch build uses --force-resolved-versions (aliases --disable-automatic-resolution, --only-use-versions-from-resolved-file), and git diff --exit-code -- Package.resolved runs after any plain build. The flag alone passed (exit 0) on a warm scratch dir with the file deleted.
SW-PKG-D03: repos that ship a binary, app, container or service track Package.resolved. Library-only and SDK-library repos gitignore it. A library that commits it for an Xcode workspace is tolerated.

SW-PKG-D01: published libraries use from: or a half-open range. Never exact:, branch:, revision: or a closed range (the planted closed range resolved 2.0.0; a versioned package with a branch dependency fails resolve, exit 1).

SW-PKG-D06/D08: macro and plugin libraries declare a multi-major half-open swift-syntax range such as "600.0.0"..<"606.0.0". from:, exact:, branch: and -latest/-prerelease bounds are leaf-tool-only (SwiftLint, swift-testing). All 4 exact-prerelease combinations conflicted (exit 1).

SW-PKG-D07: guard swift-syntax version-specific code with #if canImport(SwiftSyntaxNNN), newest first, and build CI against the lowest declared major via a consumer root exact: pin. Unguarded InlineArrayTypeSyntax failed at 600.0.1 (exit 1); the guarded twin passed.

SW-PKG-D11/D10: traits: ["X"] on a dependency replaces the defaults, so write [.defaults, "X"]. Traits are additive, default-empty unless most adopters want them, and CI runs --enable-all-traits and --disable-default-traits (a planted error behind #if Zed: default exit 0, all-traits exit 1).

SW-PKG-D09: every reference to a trait-gated or macro dependency carries condition: .when(traits:). A gated dependency is never fetched while its trait is off (unreachable URL, exit 0), but one ungated reference makes it fetch (exit 1).

SW-PKG-D13/D14: no .product(name: "_...") (planted minor bump: renamed product and changed signature both broke, the public product did not). swift-crypto is declared "1.0.0" ..< "6.0.0"; single-major or stale ..<"5.0.0" forms conflict with any 5.x sibling (exit 1).
surprises: --force-resolved-versions passes (exit 0) on a warm scratch dir even with Package.resolved deleted; it only errors on a cold scratch. The three-part gate (tracked check, fresh scratch, git diff drift check) exists because of this.

originHash is only rewritten when a pin changes (Workspace+ResolvedPackages.swift:49-72), and --force-resolved-versions never reads it. A stale hash is normal, relaxing exact: to from: did not move the pin, and raising one requirement did not move unrelated pins. The map's 'silent re-resolution' wording is too strong.

The audit says only tuist enforces the lock. containerization does too, through the alias --disable-automatic-resolution (Makefile:28, linux-build.yml:51,60, build-dist-x86_64.sh:160), and sourcekit-lsp exposes the option. None of the 10 tracked-lockfile repos runs a git diff drift check.

swift-syntax prebuilts are default-on in 6.4 but keyed to the host distro (ubuntu noble/jammy/focal, fedora 39/41, amazonlinux2, rhel9, debian12; PrebuiltLibrary.swift:154-278). The swift:6.4 image is Ubuntu 26.04 'resolute', so prebuilts silently do nothing there. 'Exact prerelease defeats prebuilts' stays an unverified inference. 'The swift-syntax cost is pin policy, not compile time' needs the distro caveat.

from: "605.0.0-latest" (swift-testing's idiom) makes a range-pinned sibling resolve to the newest prerelease, because a range admits prereleases once any bound carries a prerelease identifier (VersionSetSpecifier.swift:541-560). It then conflicts with any plain from: 604 package.

swift-crypto 5.0.0 (September 2026) makes the corpus ..<"5.0.0" form in containerization stale, and the README range is now "1.0.0" ..< "6.0.0". A typo'd trait flag (#if Zedd) is silently false even under --enable-all-traits, so no compiler gate covers trait names. SwiftPM 6.3/6.4 prune trait-gated dependencies ahead of the SE-0450 text.

top_rules: SW-ERR-01: public API declares plain `throws`; concrete `throws(T)` only for internal code, registered closed domains (errno-style struct) or Embedded. Check: grep -rPzo K6 (red rc=0, twin rc=1).
SW-ERR-02/03: forward closure errors with `throws(E)`, not `rethrows`, and annotate typed closures (`{ x throws(E) in }`); inference does not exist on 6.4 or 6.3.3.
SW-ERR-05: a function that uses async let, task groups or Task { } is declared untyped `throws` (or folds each child into Result<T,E>); never `error as! E`.
SW-ERR-07: the public error domain is one struct with an open `Code` struct, `message` and `cause: (any Error)?`; a public error enum needs `@nonexhaustive` from its first release.
SW-ERR-08: attach the cause (`cause: error`), never stringify it (`throw X("failed: \(error)")`); grep K7 catches it.
SW-ERR-09/10: every error conforms to CustomStringConvertible (plus LocalizedError returning the same text when Foundation/UI may read it); never build user text from `localizedDescription`.

SW-ERR-13/14: no empty or log-only catch and no `try?` on write/remove/copy/createDirectory/decode; allow-list is a comment in the catch body or `try? /* swallow-ok: reason */`. K1-K3 plus SwiftLint no_empty_block all went red on the plants.

SW-ERR-15: exactly one layer logs an error, the one that ends it (entry point, response-converting handler, continuing loop); lower layers add `cause:` and throw. Three layers printed 3 lines for 1 failure.
surprises: FullTypedThrows is not an upcoming feature on 6.4 or 6.3.3: `.enableUpcomingFeature("FullTypedThrows")` builds rc=0 and does nothing, the experimental form errors with 'cannot be enabled in production compiler', and only -Werror StrictLanguageFeatures exposes it. The map and SE-0413 still read as if it were pending.

Typed errors are erased by async let, withThrowingTaskGroup and Task, and by rethrows. On 6.4 only map, filter, mapValues, Optional.map and Dictionary(grouping:) keep a typed closure error; reduce, forEach, sorted, contains(where:) and 11 more erase it. 6.3.3 keeps only 3. SW-IO-FD-02: never re-encode a received JSON document to compute its digest; hash the received bytes (containerization ImageStore+Export.swift:130 violates this).

SW-IO-FD-04: parse digests over utf8 bytes with an algorithm allow-list, lowercase ASCII hex and exact length, and compare parsed values, never raw strings or .lowercased() ==; Character ranges accepted b+U+0308 and d+ZWJ.
SW-IO-FD-06: protocol text is parsed on utf8 bytes, because CRLF is one Character and "a:\u{301}b" has no ':' under split/firstIndex(of:).

SW-IO-FD-07/08/09: libraries import FoundationEssentials behind canImport with a Foundation fallback, never depend on the swift-foundation package, and every URLSession file guards FoundationNetworking (Linux error: type 'URLSession' (aka 'AnyObject') has no member 'shared').

SW-IO-FD-10/11: set dateEncodingStrategy and dateDecodingStrategy explicitly (the default encodes -978307200 for Unix 0), and add Codable fields via decodeIfPresent in a custom init(from:), because a Swift default value does not make a synthesized decoder optional.
SW-IO-FD-12/13: machine output never uses .formatted(), NumberFormatter, DateFormatter or Locale.current, and directory listings are sorted by UTF-8 bytes before reaching output or a digest.

SW-IO-FD-14: durations and timeouts use ContinuousClock (the Task.sleep default; CLOCK_BOOTTIME on Linux), SuspendingClock only for awake time, Date only for wall timestamps; grep for timeIntervalSince( and DispatchTime.now.
surprises: Planted red (e) did not go red: swift-foundation hard-codes Locale.current to en_001 on non-Darwin (Locale_Cache.swift:302-315), so LANG/LC_ALL=de_DE.UTF-8 changed nothing (cmp identical). The real Linux hazard is that .formatted() yields '1,234.5' and '14/11/2023', and that only Darwin follows user preferences (unverified: read only).

import Foundation silently changes String overload behaviour: "a
b".contains("
") is true with Foundation and false stdlib-only; CRLF is a single Character so split(separator:"
") yields one element.

Swift Regex digest in swift-container-plugin (ImageReference.swift:287) fails closed on combining marks but accepts uppercase [A-F], which OCI says MUST NOT be used; Character-range and isHexDigit versions accept b+U+0308, d+ZWJ and fullwidth U+FF41.
.sortedKeys reproduces the RFC 8785 sample byte for byte yet is not JCS: UTF-8 vs UTF-16 key order for non-BMP keys, -0 vs 0, and 1.2345678901234568e+20 vs 123456789012345680000.

Canonically-equivalent JSON member names (e-acute vs e+U+0301) collapse silently to one entry when decoded into [String: T] (count=1), and a dictionary literal with both crashes; this is a data-loss and signature-confusion vector no existing audit mentions.

Synthesized Decodable requires a property that has a Swift default value (keyNotFound on old documents); FoundationEssentials also lacks String(format:), trimmingCharacters, exit() and Process; and containerization re-encodes an OCI index with a bare JSONEncoder() at ImageStore+Export.swift:130, an in-corpus violation of the hash-received-bytes rule.

SW-IO-04 — Libraries import FoundationEssentials under canImport with Foundation fallback; hex via table lookup; never depend on the swift-foundation package (SHOULD)
SW-IO-05 — New code spawns processes with swift-subprocess; Foundation.Process only as commented legacy or file-redirecting test helper (MUST)
SW-IO-06 — Depend on swift-subprocess from: "1.0.1" (tools 6.2, traits: []); never exact: or a 0.x range (MUST)
SW-IO-07 — Check terminationStatus at every run call site; a non-zero exit is a result, not a throw (MUST)

SW-IO-13 — Parse digests over utf8 bytes into a value type, lowercase hex only, compare parsed values (MUST)
SW-IO-14 — Set dateEncodingStrategy/dateDecodingStrategy explicitly on every coder that touches a Date (MUST)
SW-IO-15 — Keep .formatted(), NumberFormatter, DateFormatter and Locale.current out of machine output (MUST)
SW-IO-16 — Use ContinuousClock for elapsed time, Date only for wall timestamps; no Date() subtraction (SHOULD)

SW-IO-18 — The durable helper is temp-in-same-dir, fchmod, fsync, checked close, rename, fsync(dir), unlink on failure; verify with strace (MUST)
SW-IO-19 — Publish CAS blobs by stage, hash-while-writing, verify, link() with EEXIST as success, 0444, fsync file and dir (MUST)

SW-IO-22 — Use flock on a lock file, not a create-exclusive PID file, for cross-process locks (SHOULD)

SW-IO-24 — Run the Configuration you mutated and prove environment overrides with a sentinel test (MUST)
SW-IO-25 — Legacy Process: drain every Pipe concurrently, never waitUntilExit before draining, merge the environment (MUST)

SW-IO-27 — Treat a cancelled run() and an early-returning .sequence body as outcomes, not errors (SHOULD)
SW-IO-28 — Evolve persisted Decodables with custom init(from:) and decodeIfPresent; 64-bit ids never through Double (SHOULD)
SW-IO-29 — Parse protocol text on utf8 bytes after an ASCII check; String/Character ops are for human text (SHOULD)
SW-IO-30 — Hash the exact bytes received or written; never re-encode a decoded document to compute its digest (MUST, reading heuristic)

The real deterministic deadlock is `Task {}` inheriting @MainActor in main.swift; the pool is core-count wide (31 ok, 32 hang). The brief's expected red did not reproduce.

concurrency/tasks-and-cancellation: `try? await Task.sleep` inside a loop becomes a hot spin after cancel (about 18,000 iterations in 500 ms) and never ends; `for await` over a cancelled AsyncStream returns normally, indistinguishable from completion.

concurrency/tasks-and-cancellation: The containerization Timeout.run shape (also the common agent shape) returns only after blocking work finishes (4000 ms for a 1 s limit) and reports CancellationError; a continuation race returns on time but orphans the work. io/subprocess-contract: Returning from a .sequence body never stops the child. run() blocked the full 2.0 s for 'sleep 2'. On 1.0.0 the early exit also leaks one fd per call (delta=50 over 50 runs), invisible to code that always drains.

io/subprocess-contract: The Process pipe-deadlock threshold is the writer's, not Foundation's. This image's uutils head/yes/cat/dd raise the pipe to 1 MiB, so a naive 'head -c' reproducer hangs only above 1 MiB. A plain write(2) writer hangs at exactly 65,537 bytes.
